questions.question: How does the Vidhan Parishad elect its chairman?

options.text: Elected by members of the Lok Sabha
Elected by members of the Vidhan Parishad

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Elected by members of the Vidhan Parishad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 182** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Legislative Council** (Vidhan Parishad) of every state that has such a council must choose two of its members to serve as the **Chairman** and **Deputy Chairman**.
 
• The **Chairman** is elected by the members of the **Vidhan Parishad** from among themselves through a process of internal voting, ensuring the **independence** of the legislature from the executive branch.
 
• The tenure of the **Chairman** is co-terminus with their membership in the council; they must vacate the office if they cease to be a member of the **Vidhan Parishad**.
 
• Unlike the **Rajya Sabha** at the Union level, where the **Vice-President of India** acts as the **Ex-officio Chairman**, the **Vidhan Parishad** does not have an ex-officio presiding officer; the leader must be an elected or nominated member of that specific house.
 
• The **Chairman** can be removed from office by a resolution passed by a **majority of all the then members** of the Council, provided a **14-day notice** has been given.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nominated by the Governor**: This is incorrect because the **Governor** only nominates 1/6th of the total members of the **Vidhan Parishad** from fields like **Literature, Science, Art, Cooperative Movement, and Social Service**. The **Governor** does not select the presiding officer.
 
• **Appointed by the President**: The **President of India** is the head of the **Union Executive** and has no constitutional role in the election or appointment of the presiding officers of a **State Legislature**.
 
• **Elected by members of the Lok Sabha**: The **Lok Sabha** is the lower house of **Parliament** and is entirely separate from the **State Legislative Council**. Members of **Parliament** (MPs) do not participate in the internal elections of the **State Vidhan Parishad**.
 
• **Powers of the Chairman**:
 
 
• The **Chairman** presides over the sittings of the Council and maintains **order and decorum** for the conduct of business.
 
• They have the power to exercise a **casting vote** in the case of a tie, although they normally do not vote in the first instance.
 
• The **Chairman** determines the **disqualification** of a member of the Council on the grounds of defection under the **Tenth Schedule** of the **Constitution**.

questions.question: Which factor led to the Mysore rebellion of 1830–31 against the restored Wodeyar administration?

options.text: Expansion of irrigation that reduced the cost of agricultural dues.
Protectionist policies designed to shield peasants from levies.
Increased revenue pressure that ultimately burdened cultivators.
Reduction in policing that strengthened the power of local chiefs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increased revenue pressure that ultimately burdened cultivators**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mysore Rebellion of 1830-31**, famously known as the **Nagar Rebellion**, was a significant peasant uprising against the administration of **Mummadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar III**.
 
• After the **Fourth Anglo-Mysore War** in **1799**, the British restored the **Wodeyar Dynasty**, but the state was bound by a **Subsidiary Alliance** treaty requiring a massive annual tribute of **7 lakh Pagodas** to the **British East India Company**.
 
• To meet these heavy financial demands, the administration utilized the **Sharat system**, a corrupt revenue-farming practice where the right to collect land revenue was auctioned to the highest bidders, known as **Amildars**.
 
• These **Amildars** frequently engaged in **extortion** and used **coercive methods** to squeeze maximum revenue from the **Ryots** (cultivators) to ensure their own profits after paying the state share.
 
• The financial distress was further aggravated by **administrative mismanagement** and the lavish lifestyle of the court, leading to an unbearable **tax burden** on the rural population, which eventually ignited the revolt in the **Nagar province**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mummadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar III**:

 
 
• He was the ruler of **Mysore** from **1799** to **1868**, though the rebellion led to his effective loss of administrative power.
 
• In **1831**, citing **maladministration** and the failure to maintain internal peace, **Governor-General Lord William Bentinck** invoked the treaty terms to take over the state administration.
 
 
 
• **British Commission Rule (1831-1881)**:
 
 
• Following the rebellion, **Mysore** was placed under the governance of **British Commissioners**, most notably **Mark Cubbon**, who served from **1834** to **1861**.
 
• This period saw the introduction of **systematic land surveys**, judicial reforms, and the abolition of the **Sharat system** to stabilize the economy.
 
• The kingdom was finally returned to the **Wodeyar family** in **1881** during an event known as the **Rendition of Mysore**.

questions.question: What is the title of the book, released in April 2025 in New Delhi, that compiles Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s speeches on culture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskriti Ka Panchva Adhyay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book titled **Sanskriti Ka Panchva Adhyay** (The Fifth Chapter of Culture) was released in **April 2025** in **New Delhi**, serving as a significant documentation of India’s contemporary cultural journey.
 
• The publication is a curated compilation of various speeches delivered by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, focusing on the themes of **cultural resurgence**, **national heritage**, and the restoration of **civilizational pride**.
 
• The title is strategically chosen as a tribute to the legendary literary work **Sanskriti Ke Char Adhyay** (Four Chapters of Culture) authored by the renowned **Rashtrakavi Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar'** in 1956.
 
• The book encapsulates the vision of **Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi** (Development along with Heritage), highlighting key initiatives such as the **Kashi Vishwanath Dham**, **Mahakal Lok**, and the construction of the **Shree Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir**.
 
• It serves as a thematic continuation of India’s cultural history, positioning the current era’s efforts in **decolonizing the Indian mindset** as the vital **Fifth Chapter** of the nation's evolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Contextual Significance**:

 
 
• **Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar'**: His original four chapters explored the synthesis of Indian culture through the **Vedic era**, **Buddhist influence**, **Islamic contact**, and **British impact**.
 
• **Fifth Chapter Concept**: PM Modi’s speeches emphasize a fifth phase characterized by **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** and the global projection of **Indian Soft Power** through **Yoga**, **Ayurveda**, and the **G20 Presidency**.
 
• **Cultural Diplomacy**: The book highlights the successful **repatriation of over 200 ancient idols** and artifacts from foreign countries to their original locations in India.
 
• **Panch Pran**: A core theme involves the Prime Minister’s **Panch Pran** (Five Pledges), particularly the goal to remove any trace of colonial slavery and take pride in our roots.

questions.question: In June 2025, which major summit was hosted for the first time by the Netherlands in The Hague (24–25 June)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NATO Summit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2025 NATO Summit** is officially scheduled to be held in **The Hague**, Netherlands, from **June 24 to June 26, 2025**.
 
• This event represents a historic milestone as it is the **first time** the Netherlands will host a formal summit of the **North Atlantic Treaty Organization** since the alliance was founded in **1949**.
 
• The summit will take place at the **World Forum** in The Hague, a city globally recognized as the **International City of Peace and Justice**.
 
• Leaders from the **32 NATO member states** will gather to discuss critical security issues, including the alliance's long-term deterrence and defense posture, as well as ongoing geopolitical conflicts.
 
• The hosting of the summit in the Netherlands highlights the country's strategic role within the **transatlantic alliance** and its commitment to international security cooperation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization)**:

 
 
• Founded by the **Washington Treaty** on **April 4, 1949**, to provide collective security against the Soviet Union.
 
• The principle of **collective defense** is enshrined in **Article 5**, stating that an attack against one member is an attack against all.
 
• The organization is headquartered in **Brussels, Belgium**, with **Mark Rutte** (former Dutch Prime Minister) designated to serve as the **Secretary General** starting in late 2024.
 
 
 
• **G7 Summit**:
 
 
• An annual meeting of the leaders of the world's most advanced economies, including **Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States**.
 
• The **51st G7 summit** in **2025** is scheduled to be hosted by **Canada**, not the Netherlands.
 
 
 
• **ASEAN Summit**:
 
 
• A biannual meeting of the **Association of Southeast Asian Nations**, focusing on economic, political, and security issues in the Southeast Asian region.
 
• Since the Netherlands is a European nation and not a member of this regional bloc, it does not host the primary **ASEAN Summit**.

questions.question: Oxidation in a redox reaction involves which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electrons lost**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxidation** is a fundamental chemical process in **Redox reactions** defined as the **loss of one or more electrons** by a chemical species (atom, ion, or molecule).
 
• When a substance undergoes oxidation, its **oxidation state** or **oxidation number** increases, indicating a higher state of positive charge or a lower state of negative charge.
 
• In a chemical equation, oxidation is represented as a **half-reaction** where electrons appear on the product side, such as Zn rightarrow Zn²⁺ + 2e^− , where **Zinc** is oxidized.
 
• The species that undergoes oxidation acts as a **reducing agent** because it provides the electrons that reduce another substance in the reaction.
 
• The concept originally meant the addition of **oxygen** to a compound, but the modern **electronic theory of valency** expanded it to include any reaction involving the transfer of electrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrons gained**:

 
 
• This process is called **Reduction**, which always occurs simultaneously with oxidation in **redox** systems.
 
• It leads to a **decrease** in the oxidation number of the atom or ion.
 
• Common mnemonics used to remember these processes are **OIL RIG** (Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain) and **LEO says GER** (Loss of Electrons is Oxidation, Gain of Electrons is Reduction).
 
 
 
• **Protons Gained and Lost**:
 
 
• Transfer of protons (H⁺ ions) is the defining characteristic of **Bronsted-Lowry acid-base reactions**.
 
• Unlike electrons, protons are located in the **atomic nucleus**; their gain or loss would result in **nuclear transmutations** or changes in the identity of the element, which does not happen in standard chemical **redox reactions**.

questions.question: वर्ष 1952 से राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों को आवंटित राज्य सभा सीटों की संख्या में उतार-चढ़ाव के लिए कौन-से कारक उत्तरदायी रहे हैं?

options.text: राज्यों का पुनर्गठन और नए राज्यों का गठन

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**राज्यों का पुनर्गठन और नए राज्यों का गठन**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• भारतीय संविधान की **चौथी अनुसूची** प्रत्येक राज्य और केंद्र शासित प्रदेश के लिए **राज्यसभा (राज्यों की परिषद)** में सीटों के आवंटन का विवरण प्रदान करती है।
 
• वर्ष **1952** में राज्यसभा के गठन के बाद से, सीटों के वितरण में होने वाले परिवर्तनों का प्राथमिक कारण भारत के राजनीतिक मानचित्र में हुआ बदलाव है, जिसे **राज्यों का पुनर्गठन** कहा जाता है।
 
• **राज्य पुनर्गठन अधिनियम, 1956** एक ऐतिहासिक कानून था जिसने भाषाई आधार पर राज्यों की सीमाओं को फिर से परिभाषित किया, जिससे कई पूर्ववर्ती राज्यों की सीटों का पुनर्वितरण हुआ।
 
• जब भी संसद किसी नए राज्य का गठन करती है या मौजूदा राज्यों की सीमाओं में परिवर्तन करती है, तो वह संविधान के **अनुच्छेद 4** के तहत चौथी अनुसूची में संशोधन करती है ताकि सीटों का आवंटन जनसंख्या के अनुपात में सुनिश्चित किया जा सके।
 
• उदाहरण के लिए, वर्ष **2000** में **छत्तीसगढ़, उत्तराखंड और झारखंड** के निर्माण और वर्ष **2014** में **तेलंगाना** के गठन के कारण संबंधित मूल राज्यों (मध्य प्रदेश, उत्तर प्रदेश, बिहार और आंध्र प्रदेश) की राज्यसभा सीटों को विभाजित और पुन: आवंटित किया गया था।
 
• हाल ही में, **जम्मू और कश्मीर पुनर्गठन अधिनियम, 2019** के माध्यम से राज्य को केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में बदलने से भी राज्यसभा सीटों की स्थिति प्रभावित हुई है।

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **राज्यसभा की संरचना और कार्य:**

 
 
• संविधान के **अनुच्छेद 80** के अनुसार, राज्यसभा की अधिकतम सदस्य संख्या **250** निर्धारित है, जिसमें **238** निर्वाचित सदस्य और **12** राष्ट्रपति द्वारा मनोनीत सदस्य शामिल होते हैं।
 
• वर्तमान में सदन की कुल संख्या **245** है। राज्यसभा के सदस्यों का चुनाव राज्य विधानसभाओं के **निर्वाचित सदस्यों** द्वारा **एकल संक्रमणीय मत** के माध्यम से आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व प्रणाली द्वारा किया जाता है।
 
• राज्यसभा एक **स्थायी निकाय** है जिसे भंग नहीं किया जा सकता है; इसके **एक-तिहाई (1/3)** सदस्य प्रत्येक दूसरे वर्ष सेवानिवृत्त होते हैं और प्रत्येक सदस्य का कार्यकाल **6 वर्ष** का होता है।
 
• सीटों का आवंटन मुख्य रूप से प्रत्येक राज्य की **जनसंख्या** पर आधारित होता है, जिसके कारण अधिक जनसंख्या वाले राज्यों (जैसे उत्तर प्रदेश) के पास कम जनसंख्या वाले राज्यों (जैसे सिक्किम) की तुलना में अधिक सीटें होती हैं।

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT influence the horizontal distribution of air pressure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ocean salinity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Air Temperature** is the most significant factor affecting horizontal pressure distribution; when air is heated, it expands, becomes less dense, and rises, creating **Low Pressure** areas, whereas cold air contracts and creates **High Pressure**.
 
• The **Presence of water vapour** influences pressure because moist air is lighter than dry air; since the molecular weight of **water vapour** is less than that of nitrogen and oxygen, humid air exerts less pressure than dry air.
 
• **Earth’s Rotation** acts as a dynamic factor that redistributes air through the **Coriolis Force**, leading to the formation of distinct pressure belts such as the **Sub-tropical Highs** and **Sub-polar Lows**.
 
• **Ocean Salinity** refers to the concentration of dissolved salts in seawater, which determines **ocean water density** and **thermohaline circulation**, but it has no direct physical impact on the horizontal weight or distribution of the **atmosphere**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmospheric Pressure** is the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air column above a location, measured using a **Barometer** in units like **Millibars (mb)** or **Pascals**.

 
 
• **Isobars**: These are lines on a map connecting places with equal air pressure at sea level; the spacing of **isobars** indicates the **pressure gradient**.
 
• **Altitude**: Pressure decreases rapidly with height because the air becomes thinner and the **density** of the atmosphere decreases as we move away from the Earth’s surface.
 
• **Coriolis Effect**: This force, caused by the **Earth’s rotation**, deflects winds to the right in the **Northern Hemisphere** and to the left in the **Southern Hemisphere**, influencing global pressure patterns.
 
• **Horizontal Distribution**: This refers to the variation of pressure across latitudes, resulting in the **Equatorial Low**, **Horse Latitudes**, and **Polar Highs**.

• A **Local Area Network (LAN)** is a computer network that interconnects computers within a **limited geographic area** such as a residence, school, **CSE classroom**, or office building.
 
• The primary purpose of a LAN in an educational setting is to facilitate high-speed **resource sharing**, including files, hardware peripherals like printers, and centralized **database access** among a group of users.
 
• LANs offer significantly **higher data transfer speeds** (often ranging from **1 Gbps to 10 Gbps**) and lower latency compared to Wide Area Networks, which is critical for real-time **collaborative group projects**.
 
• The physical connection in a LAN is typically established using **Ethernet cables** (Twisted Pair) or wireless access points (**WLAN**), ensuring that all connected nodes remain within the **same physical infrastructure**.
 
• In a **CSE classroom** scenario, the network allows for the **direct transfer** of data packets between local workstations without the need for external routing over the public internet.

• **Personal Area Network (PAN)**:

 
 
• Uses technologies like **Bluetooth** for short-range pairing, typically limited to a range of **10 meters** for personal devices.
 
 
 
• **Wide Area Network (WAN)**:
 
 
• Spans large distances, such as **continents** or the entire globe, connecting **global internet servers** through fiber optics or **leased lines**.
 
 
 
• **Satellite Communication**:
 
 
• Designed for **remote areas** where terrestrial cables cannot reach; it involves transmitting signals to **orbiting satellites**, which is not standard for local classroom file sharing due to high **propagation delay**.
 
 
 
• **Metropolitan Area Network (MAN)**:
 
 
• Covers a larger area than a LAN, such as an **entire city** or a large university campus, typically interconnecting multiple LANs.

questions.question: How did the Rangarajan Group recommend updating the poverty line in the future?

options.text: By using the Fisher Index with data from NSSO
By removing the concept of poverty line altogether
By relying on the National Accounts Statistics
By using a relative poverty measure compared to an absolute measure

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By using the Fisher Index with data from NSSO**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rangarajan Committee**, officially known as the **Expert Group to Review the Methodology for Measurement of Poverty**, was constituted in **2012** and submitted its report in **2014**.
 
• To ensure the **poverty line** remains relevant over time, the group recommended updating it using the **Fisher Index**, which is the geometric mean of the **Laspeyres** and **Paasche** price indices.
 
• This recommendation aimed to address the **substitution bias** inherent in single-index methods, providing a more balanced reflection of price changes across the **consumption basket**.
 
• The primary data source identified for this update is the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**, specifically its quinquennial **Consumer Expenditure Surveys**.
 
• The group also transitioned the data collection methodology to the **Modified Mixed Recall Period (MMRP)**, which tracks expenditure over 7 days, 30 days, and 365 days for different commodity groups to improve data reliability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fisher Index Calculation**:

 
 
• The formula is expressed as PF = sqrt{PL times PP} , where **PL** is the Laspeyres price index and **PP** is the Paasche price index.
 
• It is considered an **ideal index** in economics because it satisfies both the **time reversal test** and the **factor reversal test**.
 
 
 
• **Role of NSSO**:
 
 
• The **NSSO** (now part of the **National Statistical Office**) conducts nationwide surveys on socio-economic indicators.
 
• Its **Consumer Expenditure Survey** is the fundamental tool for estimating the **poverty ratio** in India, measuring **Monthly Per Capita Expenditure (MPCE)**.
 
 
 
• **Rangarajan vs. Tendulkar Committee**:
 
 
• The **Tendulkar Committee** (2009) had moved away from **calorie-based** anchoring, but the **Rangarajan Committee** reintroduced a normative food basket alongside expenditures on **education, clothing, and house rent**.
 
• Rangarajan's methodology resulted in a higher poverty line: **Rs 972** for rural areas and **Rs 1407** for urban areas (at 2011-12 prices).

questions.question:
Which statement is True or False regarding a computer's characteristics?

(i) Accuracy guarantees zero errors in output, even with flawed input.

(ii) No IQ means a computer cannot perform tasks without explicit instructions from the user or programmer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i) False, (ii) True**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Accuracy** in computing refers to the degree of precision with which calculations are performed. While a computer is capable of performing millions of calculations with 100% accuracy, it follows the **GIGO (Garbage In, Garbage Out)** principle. This means if the **Input Data** provided by the user is incorrect or flawed, the resulting output will also be incorrect. A computer cannot automatically correct human errors in data entry or logic. *Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.*
 
• The characteristic of **No IQ (Intelligence Quotient)** signifies that a computer is a machine with no **Independent Thinking** or decision-making power. It lacks the **Intuition** and **Wisdom** possessed by humans. Every task a computer executes is the result of a pre-defined set of **Instructions** or **Algorithms** provided by a **Programmer** or user. Without these instructions, the **Hardware** remains idle. *Hence, statement (ii) is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other fundamental **Characteristics of Computers** include:

 
 
• **Speed**: Computers can process data at incredible rates, often measured in **MIPS (Millions of Instructions Per Second)** or **BIPS (Billions of Instructions Per Second)**.
 
• **Diligence**: Unlike humans, a computer does not suffer from **Fatigue**, lack of concentration, or **Boredom**. It can perform repetitive tasks for long durations with the same level of **Reliability**.
 
• **Versatility**: A computer is capable of performing various types of tasks simultaneously, from complex **Scientific Calculations** to **Multimedia** playback and **Database Management**.
 
• **Storage**: Computers have the capacity to store vast amounts of data in **Secondary Storage** devices like **Hard Disk Drives (HDD)** and **Solid State Drives (SSD)** for future retrieval.

questions.question: Which of the following traditions are the two major streams of Indian classical music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindustani and Carnatic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian classical music is globally recognized for its two primary branches: the **Hindustani** tradition of **North India** and the **Carnatic** tradition of **South India**.
 
• Both systems are fundamentally based on the twin pillars of **Raga** (the melodic structure) and **Tala** (the rhythmic cycle), and they share the basic scale of seven notes known as **Sapta Swara** (Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni).
 
• The **Hindustani** system was significantly influenced by **Persian** and **Islamic** musical elements during the medieval period, leading to the development of various **Gharanas** or schools of music such as **Gwalior**, **Agra**, and **Kirana**.
 
• The **Carnatic** system remained largely independent of foreign influences, maintaining a more traditional and composition-heavy approach rooted in the **Temple** culture of **Southern India**.
 
• Ancient texts like the **Natya Shastra** by **Bharata Muni** (circa 200 BCE – 200 CE) and the **Sangeeta Ratnakara** by **Sarngadeva** (13th century) serve as the common theoretical foundation for both streams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Music**

 
 
• Focuses heavily on improvisation and the specific **emotional mood** associated with the time of day or season.
 
• Key vocal forms include **Dhrupad**, **Khyal**, **Thumri**, and **Tappa**.
 
• Standard instruments include the **Sitar**, **Sarod**, **Bansuri**, and **Tabla**.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music**
 
 
• Highly structured and revolves around the **Melakarta** system, which classifies 72 parent ragas.
 
• The **Trinity of Carnatic Music**—**Tyagaraja**, **Muthuswami Dikshitar**, and **Syama Sastri**—is credited with the golden age of this tradition in the 18th century.
 
• Common instruments include the **Saraswati Veena**, **Violin**, **Mridangam**, and **Ghatam**.
 
 
 
• **Distinction from Other Traditions**
 
 
• **Tribal Folk** and **Bhakti** traditions are categorized as regional or devotional music rather than formal classical systems with codified theory.
 
• **Western Classical Music** is a distinct system based on **Harmony** and **Polyphony**, contrasting with the purely **Melodic** nature of Indian classical music.

• Swami **Dayanand Saraswati** founded the **Arya Samaj** on **April 7, 1875**, in **Bombay**, with the primary objective of reforming **Hinduism** by returning to the original teachings of the **Vedas**.
 
• A hallmark of **Arya Samaj** meetings was the **gender equality** displayed in religious and social spheres, which was a radical departure from the **orthodox practices** of the 19th century.

questions.question: How do antacids reduce pain during indigestion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neutralising excess stomach acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human stomach naturally produces **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** to facilitate the digestion of food and destroy harmful bacteria.
 
• **Indigestion**, or hyperacidity, occurs when the gastric glands secrete an excessive amount of **HCl**, leading to irritation, pain, and a burning sensation in the chest or abdomen.
 
• **Antacids** are medicinal compounds that are **basic** (alkaline) in nature, designed specifically to counteract this acidity.
 
• When an antacid is ingested, it undergoes a **neutralization reaction** with the excess **Hydrochloric acid** present in the stomach.
 
• The chemical interaction between the **acid** and the **base** results in the formation of **salt and water**, effectively raising the **pH level** of the stomach contents toward a neutral state.
 
• By reducing the corrosive nature of the gastric juices, antacids provide immediate **symptomatic relief** from the pain and discomfort associated with acid reflux and peptic distress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Common Chemical Constituents of Antacids:
 
 
• **Magnesium Hydroxide**: Frequently referred to as **Milk of Magnesia**, it is a mild base with a **pH of approximately 10.5**, making it highly effective for neutralizing acids.
 
• **Sodium Bicarbonate**: Known as **Baking Soda**, it reacts rapidly with **HCl** to release **Carbon dioxide (CO₂)**, providing quick relief.
 
• **Aluminum Hydroxide**: Often used in combination with magnesium salts to balance potential digestive side effects like constipation or laxation.
 
• **Calcium Carbonate**: A potent antacid that also serves as a **calcium supplement**, reacting with acid to form calcium chloride, water, and CO₂.
 
 
 
• The fundamental chemical principle applied here is **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**, which is a cornerstone of **Arrhenius acid-base theory**.
 
• While antacids treat the symptoms by **neutralizing acid**, they do not prevent the **overproduction** of acid at its source, unlike H2 blockers or proton pump inhibitors.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments to the Constitution of India allows both the centre and states to levy the Goods and Services Tax (GST)?

__
 
• The **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016**, was the landmark legislation that facilitated the implementation of the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** across India, effective from **July 1, 2017**.
 
• It introduced **Article 246A**, which provides a special provision giving both the **Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** the concurrent power to make laws with respect to goods and services tax.
 
• Before this amendment, the **Union Government** had the exclusive power to tax services and the manufacture of goods (excise), while **State Governments** had the exclusive power to tax the sale of goods (VAT/Sales Tax).
 
• The amendment established a **dual GST structure**, allowing the Centre to levy **Central GST (CGST)** and States to levy **State GST (SGST)** on a common taxable base.
 
• It also led to the insertion of **Article 279A**, which mandated the creation of the **GST Council**, a federal body chaired by the **Union Finance Minister** to oversee tax rates, exemptions, and thresholds.

• **74th Amendment, 1992**:

 
 
• This amendment provided constitutional status to **Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities)**.
 
• It added **Part IXA** and the **Twelfth Schedule** to the Indian Constitution, specifying 18 functional responsibilities for urban governance.
 
 
 
• **80th Amendment, 2000**:
 
 
• This amendment concerned the **devolution of taxes** between the Centre and the States.
 
• It implemented the recommendations of the **10th Finance Commission**, creating an alternative scheme for sharing the net proceeds of Union taxes and duties with the States.
 
 
 
• **67th Amendment, 1990**:
 
 
• This was a state-specific amendment related to the extension of **President's Rule** in **Punjab**.
 
• It amended **Article 356** to allow the extension of the emergency period in Punjab due to prevailing internal disturbances.

questions.question: The phenotype short in pea plants is expressed by which allele combination?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Mendelian genetics**, the trait for stem height in pea plants (**Pisum sativum**) is governed by a single gene that exists in two alternative forms called **alleles**.
 
• The allele for **tallness** (represented by the uppercase letter **T**) is **dominant**, meaning it expresses itself even if only one copy is present in the genotype.
 
• The allele for **shortness** or dwarfism (represented by the lowercase letter **t**) is **recessive**, meaning its expression is masked by the presence of a dominant allele.
 
• According to the **Law of Dominance**, a **recessive phenotype** like 'short' can only be physically expressed when the organism is **homozygous recessive**, meaning it carries two copies of the recessive allele.
 
• If the plant has the allele combination **tt**, there is no dominant **T** allele to inhibit the dwarf trait, resulting in a **short phenotype**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Genotypic Combinations for Height**:

 
 
• **TT (Homozygous Dominant)**: This combination results in a **tall phenotype** because both alleles code for tallness.
 
• **Tt or tT (Heterozygous)**: These combinations result in a **tall phenotype** because the dominant **T** allele masks the recessive **t** allele.
 
• **tt (Homozygous Recessive)**: This is the only combination that results in the **short phenotype**.
 
 
 
• **Important Genetic Concepts**:
 
 
• **Phenotype**: The observable physical characteristics of an organism (e.g., tall or short).
 
• **Genotype**: The actual genetic makeup or set of alleles (e.g., **TT**, **Tt**, or **tt**).
 
• **Monohybrid Cross**: When two heterozygous (**Tt**) pea plants are crossed, the offspring typically exhibit a **phenotypic ratio** of **3:1** (three tall plants for every one short plant) and a **genotypic ratio** of **1:2:1** (**TT**:**Tt**:**tt**).

questions.question: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are managed by which body according to the Constitution?

This article mandates that the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of **electoral rolls** and the conduct of all elections to the **Panchayats** shall be vested in a **State Election Commission**.
 
• Following this, the **74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, inserted **Part IXA**, dealing with **Municipalities**. **Article 243ZA** of this part specifies that the same **State Election Commission** referred to in **Article 243K** shall also manage elections to the **Municipalities**.
 
• The **State Election Commission** is headed by a **State Election Commissioner**, who is appointed by the **Governor** of the respective state. To ensure independence, the Commissioner cannot be removed from office except in a manner and on grounds similar to those of a **Judge of a High Court**.
 
• While the **Election Commission of India** (ECI) handles national and state-level legislative elections, it has no jurisdiction over the elections of local bodies, which fall strictly under the functional domain of the state-level body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Election Commission (Election Commission of India)**:

 
 
• Established under **Article 324** of the Constitution, it is a permanent and independent body.
 
• It is responsible for conducting elections to the **Lok Sabha**, **Rajya Sabha**, **State Legislative Assemblies**, **State Legislative Councils**, and the offices of the **President** and **Vice President**.
 
 
 
• **District Magistrates**:
 
 
• While the **District Magistrate** (often designated as the **District Election Officer**) plays a vital role in executing election procedures on the ground, they act under the overall supervision and guidelines of the **State Election Commission** for local polls.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha Secretariat**:
 
 
• This is an independent body that functions under the guidance of the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha**. It provides administrative support and procedural advice to the **Lower House** of Parliament but does not have any role in the conduct or management of elections.

• The **National Waterways Act, 2016** significantly expanded its scope by declaring **111 waterways** as National Waterways, aimed at promoting fuel-efficient and environment-friendly transport.

• **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)**:

• The **Fifth Schedule** of the **Constitution of India** provides special provisions for the administration and control of **Scheduled Areas** and **Scheduled Tribes** across various states.
 
• Under **Paragraph 1** of the **Fifth Schedule**, the term **State** is specifically defined to exclude the four North-Eastern states of **Assam**, **Meghalaya**, **Tripura**, and **Mizoram**.
 
• This exclusion is because these four states are governed by the **Sixth Schedule** of the Constitution, which addresses the administration of **Tribal Areas** through **Autonomous District Councils**.
 
• While the **Fifth Schedule** relies on **Tribes Advisory Councils** and the executive power of the **Governor** to regulate land and money lending, the **Sixth Schedule** grants greater legislative and judicial autonomy to tribal regions.
 
• The **President of India** has the authority to declare an area as a **Scheduled Area**, and currently, this applies to ten states including **Andhra Pradesh**, **Jharkhand**, **Chhattisgarh**, and **Odisha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sixth Schedule States**

 
 
• **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**: These states are protected under **Article 244(2)** and **Article 275(1)** to preserve the social, cultural, and linguistic identity of tribal communities.
 
• They feature **Autonomous Districts** which can make laws on land, forest, inheritance, and marriage with the **Governor**‘s assent.
 
 
 
• **Other Special Status States**
 
 
• **Nagaland**: Though a tribal state, it is governed by **Article 371A**, which protects Naga customary laws and is not part of the **Sixth Schedule**.
 
• **Manipur**: It is governed under **Article 371C**, providing for a committee of the **Legislative Assembly** consisting of members from the Hill Areas.
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**: Governed by **Article 371H**, where the **Governor** has special responsibility regarding law and order, but it is not excluded from the **Fifth Schedule** definition in the same category as the four **AMTM** states.

questions.question: What demographic shift characterizes Brazil’s transition since the 1980s?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Falling birth and death rates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Since the **1980s**, **Brazil** has undergone a rapid **demographic transition**, shifting from a period of high natural increase to a more stabilized population structure.
 
• The **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)** in **Brazil** experienced a sharp decline, falling from approximately **4.4** children per woman in **1980** to around **1.7** by **2020**, which is significantly below the **replacement level** of **2.1**.

questions.question: Which of the following was a characteristic feature of Harappan street planning?

options.text: Elevated stone causeways replacing ordinary streets
Broad circular roads radiating out from a central square
Streets intersecting at right angles forming a criss-cross pattern
Narrow zig-zag streets designed to control traffic flow

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Streets intersecting at right angles forming a criss-cross pattern**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indus Valley Civilization** (Harappan Civilization) is celebrated for its highly advanced and systematic **urban planning**, which was a unique feature among ancient societies.
 
• Major cities like **Harappa** and **Mohenjo-daro** were laid out using a **gridiron pattern**, where the primary streets ran North-South and East-West.
 
• The streets were designed to intersect at **right angles** (90 degrees), creating a distinct **criss-cross pattern** that divided the residential areas into neat rectangular or square blocks.
 
• Main roads were remarkably wide, with some measuring approximately **10 meters** (about 33 feet) in width, allowing for the easy passage of **bullock carts** and heavy traffic.
 
• This architectural discipline extended to the smaller lanes, which were also straight and planned to ensure that every house had access to the main **drainage network**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urban Infrastructure and Sanitation**:

 
 
• The Harappans implemented an elaborate **drainage system** where drains were covered with **bricks** or **stone slabs** and equipped with **cesspits** for regular cleaning.
 
• Houses were built with **burnt bricks** of a uniform **4:2:1 ratio**, a technological feat not widely seen in other contemporary civilizations like Mesopotamia.
 
 
 
• **City Zoning**:
 
 
• Most Harappan settlements were divided into two main sections: the **Citadel** (located on a raised western platform for administrative and religious buildings) and the **Lower Town** (the eastern residential area).
 
• The **Citadel** often contained important structures like the **Great Bath** in Mohenjo-daro and large **Granaries** for storing agricultural surplus.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Features**:
 
 
• The presence of **lampposts** at regular intervals suggests that the Harappans may have had a system for **street lighting**.
 
• In cities like **Lothal**, the planning also included a massive **dockyard**, indicating the civilization's prowess in maritime trade and **hydraulic engineering**.

questions.question: The quantity represented by the unit volt per ampere corresponds to which electrical unit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ohm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Ohm's Law**, the **Electric Current** (I) flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the **Potential Difference** (V) applied across its ends, provided physical conditions like **Temperature** remain constant.
 
• The mathematical expression for this relationship is **V = I × R**, where **R** represents the **Electrical Resistance** of the conductor.
 
• To find the unit of **Resistance**, the formula is rearranged as **R = V / I**. This defines **Resistance** as the ratio of **Potential Difference** to **Current**.
 
• The **SI unit** of **Potential Difference** is the **Volt** (V), and the **SI unit** of **Electric Current** is the **Ampere** (A). Therefore, the unit for resistance is **Volt per Ampere**.
 
• The **Volt per Ampere** is internationally recognized and named as the **Ohm** (symbol: Ω), named after the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm**. One **Ohm** is the resistance of a conductor such that a **Potential Difference** of one **Volt** causes a **Current** of one **Ampere** to flow through it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coulomb**:

 
 
• It is the **SI unit** of **Electric Charge**.
 
• One **Coulomb** is defined as the quantity of electricity transported in one **Second** by a current of one **Ampere** (1 C = 1 A × 1 s).
 
 
 
• **Joule**:
 
 
• It is the **SI unit** of **Work** and **Energy**.
 
• In electrical contexts, one **Joule** is the work done to move a charge of one **Coulomb** through a potential difference of one **Volt** (1 J = 1 V × 1 C).
 
 
 
• **Watt**:
 
 
• It is the **SI unit** of **Power**, representing the rate of energy consumption or transfer.
 
• Electrical power is calculated as **P = V × I**, meaning one **Watt** is equivalent to one **Volt-Ampere** or one **Joule per second**.

questions.question: Which of the following shortcut keys opens File Explorer directly in MS Windows?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Windows logo key + E**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Microsoft Windows** operating system, keyboard shortcuts are pre-defined combinations of keys that provide an alternative way to do something that you would typically do with a mouse.
 
• The **Windows logo key + E** is the dedicated system-wide shortcut used to instantly launch **File Explorer** (previously known as **Windows Explorer**).
 
• **File Explorer** is the graphical user interface (GUI) application that allows users to navigate, access, and manage files stored on **hard disk drives (HDD)**, **solid-state drives (SSD)**, and external storage devices.
 
• This shortcut is standardized across modern versions of the OS, including **Windows 7**, **Windows 8**, **Windows 10**, and **Windows 11**, making it a critical tool for **operating system efficiency**.
 
• When pressed, it usually opens the **Quick Access** or **This PC** view by default, depending on the user's system configuration settings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Functional breakdown of other key combinations:
 
 
• **Alt + E**: Historically used in many software applications to open the **Edit menu** in the **Menu Bar**.
 
• **Ctrl + E**: Commonly used within **File Explorer** to focus the **Search Box**; in web browsers like **Microsoft Edge** or **Google Chrome**, it activates the search query in the **Address Bar**.
 
• **Shift + E**: Generally used to type the **uppercase letter E** when **Caps Lock** is disabled, or as a modifier in specific **gaming** or **design software**.
 
 
 
• Other essential **Windows logo key** shortcuts:
 
 
• **Windows logo key + D**: Used to **Show/Hide the Desktop** by minimizing all open windows.
 
• **Windows logo key + L**: Used to immediately **Lock** the PC or switch accounts.
 
• **Windows logo key + R**: Opens the **Run** dialog box for executing commands or opening programs.
 
• **Windows logo key + I**: Opens the system **Settings** menu.
